blocks.text: Inkor: I don't work, she doesn't work

1- va 3-darslarda inkor oson edi: **be** bor edi va undan keyin **not** qo'yardik (I**'m not** tired, she **isn't** working). Present Simple'da esa gapda **be** yo'q: I work, she lives. **not** ni qo'yadigan joy bo'lmagani uchun yordamchi fe'l — **do** chaqiriladi: I **do not** work → I **don't** work. O'zbekchada inkor fe'lning ichida, `-ma` qo'shimchasi bilan yasaladi: ishla**ma**yman, yasha**ma**ydi. Inglizchada esa fe'l o'zgarmaydi, uning oldiga **don't** yoki **doesn't** qo'yiladi.

**he / she / it** bilan **does** ishlatiladi — **do** ning `-es` olgan shakli. 5-darsdagi **-s** endi yordamchi fe'lga «ko'chib o'tadi», shuning uchun asosiy fe'l **yalang'och** qoladi: She work**s** → She **doesn't** work («doesn't works» emas). Bitta gapda **-s** faqat bir marta bo'ladi: yo fe'lda, yo **does** da. Xuddi shunday: He **has** → He **doesn't have**; It **goes** → It **doesn't go**; She **studies** → She **doesn't study**.

items.text: **I don't drink** cold water in winter.
The children **don't go** to school on Sunday.
This lift **doesn't stop** on the third floor.

blocks.text: do — ham yordamchi, ham asosiy fe'l

**do** ning o'zi ham oddiy fe'l bo'lishi mumkin: «qilmoq» (do homework, do sport, do the shopping). Unda inkorda **do** ikki marta keladi — biri yordamchi, biri asosiy: I **don't do** my homework at night. She **doesn't do** the cooking. Bu xato emas: birinchisi inkor yasaydi, ikkinchisi «qilmoq» ma'nosini beradi.

items.text: We **don't do** much at the weekend.

blocks.text: O'zbeklar ko'pincha bu ikki inkorni aralashtiradi. Qoida oddiy: gapda **be** bo'lsa (sifat, joy, kasb, yosh, -ing) — **am not / isn't / aren't**; boshqa har qanday fe'l bo'lsa (work, like, have, go) — **don't / doesn't**. Ikkalasi birga hech qachon kelmaydi: «I'm not like», «She isn't work», «He doesn't is» — xato.

**never** («hech qachon») o'zi inkor ma'nosida, shuning uchun u bilan **don't** ishlatilmaydi: I **never** drink coffee = I **don't** drink coffee (lekin never kuchliroq). «I don't never ...» — xato: ingliz tilida bitta gapda bitta inkor bo'ladi. O'zbekchada esa ikkita inkor odatiy: «Men **hech qachon** qahva ich**ma**yman». Xuddi shunday **nobody**, **nothing** bilan ham fe'l tasdiqda turadi: **Nobody** knows. (78-dars)

O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «I not like it.» → **I don't like it.** (yordamchi fe'l kerak); «She don't speak English.» → **She doesn't speak English.**; «He doesn't works.» → **He doesn't work.** (`-s` faqat doesn't da); «He doesn't has a car.» → **He doesn't have a car.**; «I'm not agree.» → **I don't agree.**; «I don't never eat meat.» → **I never eat meat.**

Eslab qolish: **doesn't** so'zining ichida **s** bor (doe**s**n't) — u fe'lning **-s** ini «o'g'irlab olgan». Shuning uchun undan keyingi fe'lga **-s** qo'shmang: doesn't **like**, doesn't **go**, doesn't **have**.

To'liq shakl (**do not**, **does not**) rasmiy matnda yoki urg'u berilganda ishlatiladi; so'zlashuvda doim **don't**, **doesn't**. Bog'lanish: savol shakli (**Do** you ...? **Does** she ...?) — 7-dars; o'tgan zamonda inkor (I **didn't** go) — 12-dars; barcha inkorlar jamlangan holda — 43-dars.

rows: she **doesn't** work, he **doesn't** have, it **doesn't** go

examples.title: **I / you / we / they don't** + verb
examples.description: I, you, we, they va ko'plik bilan: **don't** (= do not) + fe'l. O'zbekchada inkor fe'l ichida: ishla**ma**yman, yasha**ma**ymiz.

sentences.text: **I don't eat** meat.
We **don't live** in the city centre.
My parents **don't speak** English, but they understand a little.
sentences.translation: Ota-onam ingliz tilida **gapirmaydi**, lekin biroz tushunadi.

sentences.text: You **don't need** a visa for Kazakhstan.
sentences.translation: Qozog'istonga borish uchun sizga viza **kerak emas**.

sentences.text: Sorry, **I don't understand**. Speak more slowly, please.
Many people in London **don't have** a car.
Tom and I **don't work** on Saturdays.
These shoes are nice, but they **don't fit** me.
sentences.translation: Bu tuflilar chiroyli, lekin menga **to'g'ri kelmaydi**.

sentences.text: My grandparents **don't watch** TV in the evening; they read.
sentences.translation: Bobom va buvim kechqurun televizor **ko'rishmaydi**, kitob o'qishadi.

sentences.text: Students at our university **don't pay** for the library or the gym.
sentences.translation: Universitetimiz talabalari kutubxona va sport zali uchun **pul to'lamaydi**.

examples.title: **He / she / it doesn't** + verb (no **-s**!)
examples.description: he, she, it va bitta kishi / narsa bilan: **doesn't** (= does not) + fe'l. **-s** endi doesn't da, shuning uchun asosiy fe'lga qo'shilmaydi: she **doesn't work** («doesn't works» emas).

sentences.text: My sister **doesn't drink** coffee.
Aziz **doesn't like** horror films.
She **doesn't live** here any more.
The heater in my room **doesn't work**.
This shop **doesn't sell** newspapers.
Bekzod **doesn't eat** breakfast — he only drinks tea.
It **doesn't snow** much in Tashkent in winter.
Emma's husband **doesn't cook**, so she makes dinner every day.
sentences.translation: Emmaning eri ovqat **pishirmaydi**, shuning uchun har kuni kechki ovqatni Emma tayyorlaydi.

sentences.text: My phone **doesn't take** good photos at night.
Our teacher **doesn't give** homework at the weekend, and everybody loves her for it.
sentences.translation: O'qituvchimiz dam olish kunlari uyga vazifa **bermaydi**, buning uchun hamma uni yaxshi ko'radi.

examples.title: **likes** ..., but **doesn't like** ...
examples.description: Tasdiq va inkor yonma-yon: Aziz **likes** tea, but he **doesn't like** coffee. E'tibor bering: tasdiqda **-s** fe'lda, inkorda — doesn't da.

sentences.text: Madina **likes** cats, but she **doesn't like** dogs.
I **know** his face, but **I don't know** his name.
James **speaks** French, but he **doesn't speak** German.
We **eat** a lot of fruit, but we **don't eat** many sweets.
sentences.translation: Biz ko'p meva **yeymiz**, lekin shirinlikni ko'p **yemaymiz**.

sentences.text: The café **opens** early, but it **doesn't close** late.
My son **reads** a lot, but he **doesn't read** newspapers.
Dilnoza **drives** to work; her husband **doesn't drive** at all.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza ishga mashinada **boradi**, eri esa umuman mashina **haydamaydi**.

sentences.text: In summer it **gets** very hot here, but it **doesn't rain**.
sentences.translation: Yozda bu yerda havo juda **isib ketadi**, lekin yomg'ir **yog'maydi**.

sentences.text: Tom **plays** football and tennis, but he **doesn't play** golf.
sentences.translation: Tom futbol va tennis **o'ynaydi**, lekin golf **o'ynamaydi**.

sentences.text: Children usually **love** holidays, but they **don't love** getting up early for school.
sentences.translation: Bolalar odatda ta'tilni **yaxshi ko'radi**, lekin maktab uchun erta turishni **yoqtirmaydi**.

examples.title: **doesn't have**, **doesn't do**, **doesn't go**
examples.description: Inkorda fe'l doim «yalang'och»: has → **doesn't have**, does → **doesn't do**, goes → **doesn't go**, studies → **doesn't study**. **do** asosiy fe'l bo'lsa ham: I **don't do** sport.

sentences.text: Bekzod **doesn't have** a car.
**I don't do** my homework on Friday evenings.
Grandpa **doesn't go** to bed before midnight.
My cousin **doesn't study** at university; he works in a factory.
Sarah **doesn't do** any sport, but she walks a lot.
sentences.translation: Sara hech qanday sport bilan **shug'ullanmaydi**, lekin ko'p piyoda yuradi.

sentences.text: This hotel **doesn't have** a swimming pool.
We **don't go** to the cinema very often.
Tom **doesn't try** very hard at school, unfortunately.
The number 7 bus **doesn't go** to the airport — you need the number 12.
Aziz **doesn't wash** his car himself — his father does it for him.
sentences.translation: Aziz mashinasini o'zi **yuvmaydi** — uni dadasi yuvib beradi.

examples.title: **isn't** or **doesn't**? **be** and other verbs
examples.description: Sifat, joy, kasb, yosh — **be** bilan: she **isn't** tired, I**'m not** a student. Boshqa fe'llar — **don't / doesn't** bilan: she **doesn't** work, I **don't** know. Ikkisini aralashtirmang.

sentences.text: **I'm not** hungry, and **I don't want** any food.
Aziz **isn't** a teacher; he **doesn't work** at a school.
The flat **isn't** big, and it **doesn't have** a balcony.
My parents **aren't** from Tashkent, and they **don't like** big cities.
Emma **doesn't eat** much because she **isn't** very well.
sentences.translation: Emma ko'p **ovqat yemaydi**, chunki uning mazasi **yo'q**.

sentences.text: This exercise **isn't** difficult — it **doesn't take** long.
We **aren't** rich, but we **don't need** much money.
sentences.translation: Biz boy **emasmiz**, lekin bizga ko'p pul **kerak emas**.

sentences.text: Dilnoza **isn't** at work today — she **doesn't work** on Thursdays.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza bugun ishda **emas** — u payshanba kunlari **ishlamaydi**.

sentences.text: Sorry, **I don't know** — **I'm not** from here.
Bekzod **isn't** a big fan of football, so he **doesn't watch** the matches.
sentences.translation: Bekzod futbolning katta muxlisi **emas**, shuning uchun o'yinlarni **ko'rmaydi**.

examples.title: Rules and customs: what people **don't** do
examples.description: Qoidalar va urf-odatlar haqida gapirganda ham Present Simple inkori kerak: In Uzbek homes people **don't** ..., Our school **doesn't** ...

sentences.text: In Uzbek homes people **don't wear** shoes inside.
Our school **doesn't allow** phones in class.
In Britain cars **don't drive** on the right.
My dad **doesn't let** us use phones at the dinner table.
sentences.translation: Dadam ovqat paytida telefon ishlatishimizga **ruxsat bermaydi**.

sentences.text: The shops in our village **don't open** on Sunday mornings.
Young people **don't sit** while older people are standing.
This restaurant **doesn't take** credit cards, only cash.
sentences.translation: Bu restoran kredit kartalarini **qabul qilmaydi**, faqat naqd pul.

sentences.text: Guests **don't come** with empty hands in Uzbekistan — they bring sweets or fruit.
sentences.translation: O'zbekistonda mehmonlar quruq qo'l bilan **kelmaydi** — shirinlik yoki meva olib kelishadi.

sentences.text: In the library you **don't talk** loudly.
Our football coach **doesn't accept** excuses — everybody trains, even in the rain.
sentences.translation: Futbol murabbiyimiz hech qanday bahonani **qabul qilmaydi** — hamma, hatto yomg'irda ham mashq qiladi.

examples.title: Not true! **Penguins don't fly.**
examples.description: Faktlarni inkor qilish va noto'g'ri fikrni tuzatish: Penguins **don't fly**. The sun **doesn't go** round the Earth.

sentences.text: Penguins **don't fly**, but they swim very well.
The sun **doesn't go** round the Earth.
Bananas **don't grow** in Scotland — it's too cold.
sentences.translation: Shotlandiyada banan **o'smaydi** — u yer juda sovuq.

sentences.text: Fish **don't sleep** with their eyes closed.
Money **doesn't buy** happiness, my grandmother says.
A spider **doesn't have** six legs — it has eight.
Water **doesn't freeze** at five degrees; it freezes at zero.
sentences.translation: Suv besh darajada **muzlamaydi**, nol darajada muzlaydi.

sentences.text: The Amu Darya **doesn't flow** through Tashkent.
Most cats **don't like** water, but some love it.
sentences.translation: Ko'p mushuklar suvni **yoqtirmaydi**, lekin ba'zilari uni yaxshi ko'radi.

sentences.text: Tomatoes and cucumbers **don't grow** well without sun and water.
sentences.translation: Pomidor va bodring quyosh va suvsiz yaxshi **o'smaydi**.

examples.title: Mixed: two very different brothers
examples.description: Mustahkamlash: tasdiq va inkor, **don't / doesn't**, **aren't** — ikki aka-ukaning odatlari solishtiriladi.

sentences.text: Aziz and Bekzod are brothers, but they **aren't** very similar.
sentences.translation: Aziz va Bekzod aka-uka, lekin bir-biriga unchalik **o'xshamaydi**.

sentences.text: Aziz **gets up** at six; Bekzod **doesn't get up** before ten.
sentences.translation: Aziz soat oltida **turadi**, Bekzod esa o'ndan oldin **turmaydi**.

sentences.text: Bekzod **doesn't like** sport at all.
His brother **runs** every morning and **doesn't eat** fast food.
Bekzod **plays** computer games until late and **doesn't do** his homework.
sentences.translation: Bekzod kechgacha kompyuter o'yini **o'ynaydi** va uy vazifasini **qilmaydi**.

sentences.text: Aziz **doesn't play** games — he **reads** books about history.
Their mother **says** they **don't agree** about anything.
But they **don't argue** much, and they **help** each other.
sentences.translation: Lekin ular ko'p **janjallashmaydi** va bir-biriga **yordam beradi**.

sentences.text: On Fridays they **don't stay** at home — they **visit** their grandmother together.
sentences.translation: Juma kunlari ular uyda **qolishmaydi** — birga buvisinikiga **borishadi**.

sentences.text: Nobody **understands** them, but everybody **loves** them.
sentences.translation: Ularni hech kim **tushunmaydi**, lekin hamma ularni **yaxshi ko'radi**.
